item.title: The Imitation Game: Running a Hands-On Turing Test in the Informatics Classroom
item.description: When introducing students to artificial intelligence, conversations inevitably lead back to Alan Turing’s seminal 1950 question: “Can machines think?” In traditional textbooks, the Turing Test (originally described as The Imitation Game) is frequently treated as an abstract historical anecdote: an interrogator asks questions through a teletype terminal to a hidden human and machine, trying to distinguish between the two. Simply reading a paragraph about it seldom leaves a lasting impression.
